newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTOR RACING-FORMULA ONE CIRCUS LEAVES BITTER ROW BEHIND.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FORMULA ONE CIRCUS LEAVES BITTER ROW BEHIND.

text.p: The Formula One circus flew out of Melbourne on Monday, leaving behind a furious row over a public transport strike which slashed attendance at Sunday's Australian Grand Prix.
Crowds for the season-opening race fell by one third compared to last year, causing a drop in ticket sales worth up to A@10 million (US$7.8 million), according to organisers.
The Victoria state government, which paid to bring the race to Melbourne, had predicted a A$2.9 million profit before the weekend strike took trams and buses of the streets.

An estimated 107,000 spectators went through the turnstiles at Albert Park to watch Briton David Coulthard drive a McLaren to victory, compared to a crowd of 154,000 in 1996. Victorian authorities laid on a fleet of 600 private buses to take spectators to the Albert Park street track.
Australian Prime Minister John Howard criticised trade union leaders who reportedly used free tickets to attend the race after calling the strike on Grand Prix weekend.
Howard said calling the strike was "an act of complete bloody-mindedness" but then to go to the race with free tickets was "a crowning hypocrisy".

Public transport workers' leader Leigh Hubbard, whose union is seeking a wage increase and improved working conditions, accused the government of picking an ideological fight, adding: "It is a war and the unions will use whatever tactics they think are appropriate."
